summary: case-005 (e.oz@aegean.edu): benign, confidence 0.85 per Risk Gate; no compromise signal survived critic review. F1: OWA inbox forwarding rule to internal address e.oz.archive@aegean.edu is not exfiltration. F2: 71 failures from 193.140.10.9 across 68 accounts plus one later sign-in is shared-egress background noise, not a password spray, given 188 MFA logins from that IP in 30 days.

Tune password-spray detection for shared egress IP 193.140.10.9; alert only on failures followed by a successful same-account MFA login.
Confirm with the user that e.oz.archive@aegean.edu is an intended internal archive mailbox.

risk.rationale: No surviving/confirmed findings exist for case-005. Both raised signals were investigated and rejected with verified explanations: (1) the OWA inbox forwarding rule points to an internal @aegean.edu archive address, so it is not exfiltration; (2) the 193.140.10.9 activity is shared egress with 188 distinct accounts completing MFA from that IP in 30 days, and the 71 failures across 68 accounts are background noise rather than a coordinated spray, with the later sign-in attributable to legitimate use of that shared egress. With no confirmed account-takeover chain and no unexplained residual signal, the suspicious indicators are explained away, which matches benign rather than contain/monitor/escalate. I am not dissenting from the obvious policy call, so no confirmed finding is required to override.
